summary: Iteration 76 — Phase 1: Membership Entitlements v2 + Menu/Product Option Groups (BACKEND ONLY) tested end-to-end against the shared FastAPI/MongoDB backend. Backend: 24/24 pytest cases pass (/app/backend/tests/test_iter76_membership_entitlements.py). (a) MENU option_groups — POST/PATCH/GET/BULK /api/merchant/marketplace/menu/items persist option_groups with generated group_id (grp_...) + option_id (opt_...); size/single groups have max_select forced to 1; multi keeps its max_select (verified with max_select=3); PATCH preserves group_ids when the client sends them back. (b) PRODUCT option_groups — POST/PATCH /api/merchant/marketplace/products/items accepts BOTH legacy variants and new option_groups on the same document; both persist. (c) MEMBERSHIP PLAN v2 — POST/PATCH /api/merchant/marketplace/memberships/items stores plans with schema_version=2 and entitlement_id (ent_...) generated. GET / returns member_count. Full entitlement fields round-trip: target_type, target_ids, category, included_option_ids, quantity, reset_frequency (daily/weekly/monthly/billing_cycle/total), rollover, rollover_cap, day_time, stackable, max_upcharge_cents, active. (d) CONSUMER WALLET — GET /api/shop/memberships/mine returns entitlements with ledger-backed remaining/used/period_key AND backward-compat aliases qty/period/options AND available_now (day/time). GET /api/shop/businesses/{business_id}/memberships returns items+mine correctly. (e) CLAIM FLOW — POST /api/shop/memberships/{id}/claim accepts BOTH new entitlement_id AND legacy benefit_id body fields; successful claim decrements remaining and appends to membership_redemption_ledger (verified by re-reading /mine and confirming used+1, remaining-1); unknown entitlement returns 404 benefit_not_found; exhausted entitlement (Ambreens '10% off colour services' monthly qty=1 already used=1) returns 400 code=limit_reached. (f) CONSUMER CATALOGUE — GET /api/shop/businesses/{id}/menu and /products expose option_groups on every item/product. (g) BOOT MIGRATION — sample plans read as schema_version=2 with normalized entitlements[].entitlement_id populated; the wallet reads without 500s and returns coherent used/remaining ints from the ledger (proving legacy claims were mirrored into membership_redemption_ledger). (h) REGRESSION — /api/shop/orders/quote (menu) and /api/shop/cart/quote (products, requires groups[] wrapper) both still return 200 for flat-price items without any option selection — option_groups is confirmed additive, no break. As per E1's note, checkout does NOT yet charge for selected option upcharges or apply entitlements (deferred to Phase 3) — that behaviour was not asserted. `outside_time_window` code path was NOT exercised end-to-end (would require a stripe subscription to a v2 plan with a restrictive day_time window, which is deferred); the code is well-formed and covered by unit-level day_time_allows helper.
action_items: (Phase 3) Wire CheckoutItem to accept selected_option_ids and apply option upcharges + entitlement redemption on order creation (record_redemption from services.membership_entitlements) — currently /quote and /checkout ignore option_groups selections.

(Optional/minor) The claim endpoint still uses the LEGACY `choice_labels` list to validate the `option` body param (marketplace_memberships.py:325-327). The v2 schema stores `included_option_ids` instead. On brand-new v2 plans created via the new endpoint (not migrated), `choice_labels` will be empty, so the `option_required` guard silently no-ops. Not a functional bug today but you'll want to migrate this to a real option_id validation against the target item's option_groups in Phase 3.

(Optional/minor) `_benefit_status` returns `options: e.get('choice_labels', [])` as a legacy alias. For plans created fresh via the v2 endpoint (never had choice_labels), this alias is always `[]`. Pre-v2 clients that render this list will see empty options on new plans — acceptable during Phase 1, worth noting for the client-migration checklist.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/services/membership_entitlements.py::normalize_option_groups — correctly forces max_select=1 for size/single groups (line 74) and preserves group_id/option_id when supplied (line 76 & 67). Idempotent as designed. Good.

/app/backend/services/membership_entitlements.py::migrate_memberships_v2 — idempotency is done right: (1) plans use `{'schema_version': {'$ne': 2}}` filter so a re-run touches nothing; (2) legacy claims use `led_legacy_<claim_id>` as a deterministic ledger_id with upsert+$setOnInsert, so duplicate rows are impossible on re-run. Verified by E1's manual observation (first boot: 4/5, subsequent: 0/0).

/app/backend/routes/marketplace_memberships.py::claim_benefit still validates the `option` body against `choice_labels` — a MIGRATION-ONLY legacy field. New v2 plans created via the endpoint never populate choice_labels, so the option-required guard is effectively disabled for them. This is fine now (Phase 1) but must be replaced with option_group-aware validation in Phase 3.

/app/backend/routes/marketplace_memberships.py::claim_benefit — the ledger append is fire-and-forget after the remaining check with no transaction/lock. Under concurrent claims of the same entitlement (same user, two tabs), both requests can pass the remaining>0 check and each write a row to the immutable ledger, over-drawing the allowance. Given single-user pace this is unlikely to bite, but if you care about strict per-period quantity enforcement, either (a) use a unique index on (membership_id, entitlement_id, period_key, seq) with atomic $inc-and-check, or (b) wrap in a MongoDB transaction. Flagging for Phase 3 hardening.

/app/backend/routes/marketplace_memberships.py::_benefit_status — returns entitlement fields via `**e` spread which leaks internal-only keys like `choice_labels` to the client. Minor: consider whitelisting the fields returned.

/app/backend/services/membership_entitlements.py::entitlement_remaining scans the ledger with an async for + Python sum instead of an aggregate($sum). Fine for small ledgers but will linearly slow the wallet endpoint if a single user's ledger grows large (thousands of rows). Consider `db.membership_redemption_ledger.aggregate([{$match:...}, {$group:{_id:null, used:{$sum:'$qty'}}}])`.

Sample seeded plans (Coffee Club, Unlimited Blowouts) use quantity=99 daily which reads more like 'unlimited' than the marketing 'free coffee daily' promise — could confuse QA when trying to trigger limit_reached; consider quantity=1 for daily perks in the sample data (or a dedicated smaller-cap sample entitlement).

context_for_next_testing_agent: All Phase 1 backend surfaces green. Do NOT expect option_groups to affect /quote or /checkout totals yet — that's Phase 3. When Phase 3 lands, the /quote path should accept CheckoutItem.selected_option_ids and the response should include per-item selected_options + option_upcharge_cents; also entitlements should decrement automatically on checkout success (currently only the manual /claim endpoint touches the ledger). Consumer catalogue endpoints already expose option_groups so frontends can build the picker UI now. Immutable ledger collection is `membership_redemption_ledger` — reversals append status='reversal' rows rather than deleting.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found in Phase 1.
